label: character sheets (person_v1, one call per person)

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. This is the gate of the city.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: The gate beam needs raising, but it is heavy work. Have you handled such a task before, stranger?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain keeps the gate secure. I expect evidence and discipline from anyone under my command.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: What is your business in the city, stranger? Give me a plain reason for entry.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is. State your name and business, stranger.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is not required, stranger. I keep the gate secure and judge by evidence, not promises.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now, just outside the city gate. New to town, are you? What brings you this way?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, that’s a generous offer for a quiet stretch of road. What sort of hand are you offering?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Well now, strict as a winter frost, but fair when you give him no cause to be otherwise. What brings you to asking about Roderic?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, the gate’s hard to miss. What brings you into the city?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, the sky’s doing its best. What brings you to the gate?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Well now, you needn't trust me much. I’m asking the questions, and you can judge me by whether I’m fair with your answers. What brings you to the gate?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day? Stop there. What brings you to the gate, and who are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? What for, exactly?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? Roderic keeps order, and I respect him. What brought you to ask?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Advice? Papers, or someone to vouch for you. Otherwise you’ll be turned away.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather? Fine enough. You here to pass through, or just making talk?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You needn't. Tell me who you are and what brings you to the gate.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, love, this is the inn yard, just outside the walled city. The gate’s about forty steps north, if that’s where you’re headed.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I could use a hand hauling water from the trough for the kitchen—will you do that for me?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, Roderic’s stiff as his own gate, but fair. He listens when someone he respects speaks up for a newcomer.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, the gate's about forty steps north. Captain Roderic keeps it; I couldn't say what he'll require, but he listens when a respected resident speaks up for a newcomer.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is, love. Makes the yard feel almost cheerful, even with all the work waiting.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, love, you needn’t take my word for anything just yet. I’m Hessa, and I keep the inn; tell me what’s brought you here, and we’ll see each other plain enough.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: The smithy. If you mean the town, it's outside the city gate, east along the road.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Charcoal or dry wood would help. If you bring some, I’ll put in a good word for you with the captain.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Roderic pays late, but he pays. He keeps the guards’ work coming, so I’d rather he stay patient.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Go to the gate and speak plainly to Captain Roderic. He decides who gets through; I’ve no say in it.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: What. If you're buying, speak.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You don't have to. Say what you want, and I'll judge it by what you do.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, hello! This is the smithy's yard, just by the forge—I'm Jory, Mara's apprentice. Are you from far away?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, maybe! Aunt Mara’s at the forge just four steps that way—she might have work for you. Are you handy with a hammer, or do you know some other trade?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, the captain? I don't know him well enough to say, but he must see all sorts at the gate. Have you met him?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh! The gate’s about thirty steps that way, but you’ll need to ask the guards there. Are you from far off, then?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh! It is, isn't it—and I was just thinking how fine weather makes the forge feel less like an oven. Are you from around here, or passing through?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, I don't know that you should yet! I don't know you, and you don't know me—but I can tell you what I know, and you can judge for yourself. What brought you here?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Good day. This is the carpenter’s yard, just outside the city gate. The gate is about twenty-two steps north-west.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: The gate beam needs a careful lift. If you can get the cracked bar down and raise the replacement safely into its brackets, I’ll put in a good word for you with the captain.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Roderic wants that beam raised before patience runs out. He watches the work closely, but I can't fault him for wanting it done safely.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: The gate is about twenty-two steps northwest. Roderic is the captain there; ask him about entry.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Aye, fair enough. Though this beam would be easier to lift in dry weather.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You needn't trust me on my word. Judge me by the work in front of us: a clear plan, sound measurements, and no hands on my tools without leave.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! This is the village outside the city gate. The gate lies about thirty-seven steps north-west—are you bound for the city, or just looking around?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, perhaps. What can you do that would earn its keep?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Friend, I’ve no measure of him yet. A captain who keeps the gate orderly may be worth knowing—what has he done to catch your eye?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Friend, the gate is about thirty-seven steps northwest; the captain there decides who passes. What business can you offer him?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend! Fine weather makes for better trade, I always say. Have you business by the wagon?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Friend, trust is a costly thing. What have you to offer that makes the risk worthwhile?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Stranger. This is the road below the city gate. What brings you here?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Stranger. You came up the south road. I’m watching it; what sort of help do you offer?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: I’ve seen him give orders. I won’t guess at the rest.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: You’ll need to speak with Captain Roderic at the gate, about twelve steps north. He decides who enters.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear skies, yes. You came up the south road. What brings you here?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You needn't trust me. I report what I see, and leave the rest for the captain to judge.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Hm. Village approach. What brings you here?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Hm. Not here.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Captain Roderic? Good enough. Knows his post.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Hm. Ask my captain at the gate, north from here.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hm. Weather's weather. What brings you here?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust? I don't ask for it. What brings you here?
